newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Bank of Taiwan signs $1.13bln loan for Pertamina.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Taiwan signs $1.13bln loan for Pertamina.

text.p: Taiwan's biggest state-run bank, Bank of Taiwan, on Saturday signed a protocol of intent to be the lead underwriter for a US$1.13 billion syndicated loan to Indonesian state oil company Pertamina.
The loan is to be used to finance Pertamina's eighth liquefied natural gas plant, planned for Botang in East Kalimantan, executives said at a signing ceremony in Taipei.

"The transaction represents a new milestone for the development of the Taiwan banking industry and in establishing Taiwan as a significant financing centre in the Asia-Pacific region," Bank of Taiwan president Ho Kuo-hwa told reporters.
Other underwriters include Mitsubishi Corp, Chase Manhattan Corp, Banque Indosuez, Fuji Bank, Long Term Credit Bank and Tokai Bank.
"We will also invite at least seven domestic (Taiwan) banks to participate in this loan," Ho said.
He said the local underwriters have yet to be determined.
Syndication of the financing will begin soon, with closing targetted for the end of February.
The LNG plant, planned in conjunction with Pertamina's 20-year LNG sales contract with Taiwan's state-run Chinese Petroleum Corp in 1995, would have annual capacity of 2.95 million tonnes.
Pertamina said the plant, called the Train H project, would begin construction in March 1997 and finish by September 1999.
Indonesia is the world's largest producer and exporter of liquefied natural gas.
